subject: Biology
topicDescription: Water movement, transpiration, and sugar transport.

sections.heading: Water and transpiration
sections.body: Water absorbed by roots travels through xylem to stems and leaves. Evaporation of water from leaf surfaces followed by diffusion of water vapour out through stomata is called transpiration. This water loss helps maintain an upward flow of water through the xylem. Wind, temperature, humidity, and light can affect the rate.

sections.heading: Transporting sugars
sections.body: Phloem transports dissolved sugars, especially sucrose, from sources such as photosynthesising leaves to sinks such as growing tissues and storage organs. Movement of dissolved products through phloem is called translocation. Unlike the xylem's main upward flow, phloem transport can occur in different directions in different sieve tubes.

keyTerms.definition: Loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through leaf stomata.
Movement of dissolved organic substances through the phloem.
A source supplies a substance; a sink uses or stores it.

questions.prompt: Which tissue mainly carries water from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Water and mineral ions move through xylem tissue from roots towards stems and leaves.

options: Loss of water vapour from leaves
Movement of dissolved sugars through phloem
Movement of water through the soil
questions.explanation: Phloem translocates dissolved sugars from sources to parts of the plant that use or store them.
